theory.title: Past perfect and narrative tenses
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 011. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Past perfect and narrative tenses
patterns.pattern: had + past participle / had been + -ing
examples: They had already discussed the issue.
She had been reflecting on the decision for weeks.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 011 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Wish and if only
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 012. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Wish and if only
patterns.pattern: wish / if only + past or past perfect
examples: I wish I were more patient.
If only I had asked for clarification.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

phrases.english: A key issue is how decisions are justified.
phrases.spanish: Una cuestión clave es cómo se justifican las decisiones.

phrases.english: There is more to consider than first appears.

reading.english: Read for the writer's position as well as the supporting details.

writing.english: Develop each point with a reason, an example and a measured conclusion.

speaking.english: I take that point, although I would add an important qualification.

listening.english: Listen for contrast, emphasis and the speaker's underlying intention.

content.passage: The question of 012 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 012 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Advanced relative clauses
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 013. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Advanced relative clauses
patterns.pattern: which / whose / whereby / in which
examples: The colleague, whose judgement I value, challenged the idea.
It was a decision in which everyone had a say.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

content.passage: The question of 013 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 013 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Passive forms and reporting
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 014. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Passive forms and reporting
patterns.pattern: be + past participle / it is reported that
examples: The proposal was approved after consultation.
It is widely believed that early support matters.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

content.passage: The question of 014 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 014 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Conditionals and concession
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 015. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Conditionals and concession
patterns.pattern: if / unless / provided that / although
examples: If access improves, participation will rise.
Although the plan is costly, it may be worthwhile.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

content.passage: The question of 015 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 015 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Modal deduction and speculation
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 016. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Modal deduction and speculation
patterns.pattern: must / may / might / can't have + participle
examples: The figures must have been updated.
The delay might have been caused by the weather.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 016 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Participle clauses
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 017. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Participle clauses
patterns.pattern: -ing / having + past participle
examples: Having considered both sides, she changed her mind.
Faced with criticism, he responded calmly.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. theory.title: Hedging and advanced linking
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 019. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Hedging and advanced linking
patterns.pattern: tend to / arguably / nevertheless / to some extent
examples: The proposal seems to address the main concern.
Arguably, context matters more than first impressions.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

content.passage: The question of 019 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 019 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Gerund and infinitive patterns
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 020. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Gerund and infinitive patterns
patterns.pattern: verb + -ing / verb + to-infinitive
examples: Some people avoid making assumptions.
She agreed to reconsider her view.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

phrases.english: A key issue is how decisions are justified.
phrases.spanish: Una cuestión clave es cómo se justifican las decisiones.

phrases.english: There is more to consider than first appears.
phrases.spanish: Hay más que considerar de lo que parece a primera vista.

reading.english: Read for the writer's position as well as the supporting details.
reading.spanish: Lee para identificar la postura del autor y los detalles que la respaldan.

writing.english: Develop each point with a reason, an example and a measured conclusion.
writing.spanish: Desarrolla cada punto con una razón, un ejemplo y una conclusión matizada.

speaking.english: I take that point, although I would add an important qualification.

content.passage: The question of 020 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 020 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.
